steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Crypto-key routing** in *VPNs and tunnels*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: WireGuard over IPv4 adds 60 bytes of headers. What inner MTU and TCP MSS fit a 1500-byte path?
steps.explain: WireGuard's default of 1420 also leaves room for IPv6 outer headers.

steps.title: Rebuild Crypto-key routing cold
prompt: Write `string Peer(List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> peers, string dst)` returning the peer whose AllowedIPs contain `dst` with the **longest** prefix,
or `"dropped (no peer)"`. The editor is empty, so the three helpers are not there: copy them from the shape below.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
string Peer(List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> peers, string dst)
